Subject: Marketplace private offer & unit price mapping 14 follow-up

Hi Ryan 14

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery on the BrightCart use case and a few follow-ups so we can map the pricing into an AWS Marketplace private offer:

Key points I captured from the call:
- Expected monthly token volume: ~8-12B tokens/month (edge-case spikes up to ~15B).
- Primary region: US (AWS).
- Target economics: BrightCart is looking for a unit price in the $/1M tokens range that makes sense vs. your existing spend - you mentioned a ballpark target of $600-$800 per 1M tokens.

Questions / asks for procurement mapping:
1) Can you confirm the final expected monthly volume range (low / high) for the first 12 months? We used 8-12B as a working assumption.
2) Do you want price quoted as a committed monthly quantity (reserved) or as a monthly tiered consumption price? Committed usually unlocks lower $/1M but requires a minimum monthly commitment.
3) Please confirm the AWS Account ID you want the private offer to target and whether BrightCart will accept marketplace fees applied on top of the unit price (we typically see 5-15% marketplace fees depending on the program).

Attached is a draft unit price mapping spreadsheet that shows how we translate Redwood's internal unit economics to marketplace SKUs for AWS/GCP/Azure and the approximate impact of marketplace fees. If it helps, Aditya (cc'd) can do a short walk-through on the mapping.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm volumes and preferred pricing structure (committed vs. consumption) - ideally by EOD Mon 5/3.
- We'll run a quick internal pricing sanity check and return a marketplace mapping + suggested private offer price ranges.
- If agreed, we'll draft an AWS Marketplace Private Offer and send it to your procurement for signature.

Attachments: unit_price_mapping.csv

Thanks - talk soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Marketplace private offer & unit price mapping 14 follow-up

Great - thanks for the quick confirmation and for the AWS account.

Answers to your questions and a short mapping note below. Aditya, looping you in to confirm the SKU mapping and to help quantify kernel-level optimizations that impact unit economics.

1) Quote basis: We will provide two figures in the mapping - (A) Redwood list unit price (this is what Redwood charges directly, before marketplace fees) and (B) Marketplace unit price (the actual charge on the Marketplace + typical marketplace fee range). Procurement usually wants to see both so they can reconcile to their internal PO templates.

2) Commit requirements for $600: To reach ~$600/1M tokens on AWS Marketplace private offers, we typically need a 12-month committed baseline in the 8-10B tokens/month range with modest quarterly ramp provisions. For purely consumption (no commit) pricing, the comparable unit would be closer to $900-$1,100/1M tokens.

Preliminary unit price mapping (illustrative):
- Redwood list price (hosted API, committed): $520 / 1M tokens
- Marketplace add-on (expected): +10% (marketplace fees and buyer-side surcharge) -> Marketplace unit price = ~$572 / 1M tokens
- If we apply a platform/partner fee for AWS private offer packaging (one-time), that is handled as a separate line item on the PO.

Notes:
- The numbers above assume standard sequence lengths for your workloads and the KV-caching/batching patterns we discussed. High context-length workloads or heavy non-cached generation will increase effective $/1M.
- We can provide a 12-month committed pricing worksheet that ties a committed monthly token baseline to tiered unit prices and an overall committed spend.

Attachments I'm sending: marketplace_po_template.docx (draft private offer terms + fields we need filled for procurement). Aditya - can you confirm the SKU mapping in the attached CSV and flag any SKUs that need to be split by region or instance family?

Proposed next steps:
- By Mon 5/3: BrightCart confirms commit preference (9B baseline vs. fully consumption).
- Wed 5/5: Redwood sends committed-pricing worksheet + marketplace private offer draft.
- Following review: Proc signature and start of private offer provisioning.

Thanks - I'll be available for a walk-through if you want to go line-by-line with Aditya.

Best,
Marissa
